ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The image shows a transition-state structure. On the left, R is connected to a carbon; this carbon is connected upward to H and connected to B on the right through a carbon chain. B is connected upward to R' and connected to R' on the right. Below, there is an O—OH fragment bearing a negative sign, and there is a curved arrow pointing near B. Reasoning: The problem requires ignoring the arrows and excluding all bonds involving hydrogen. Therefore, the upward C-H bond from the carbon is not counted, and the O-H bond in O—OH is also not counted. The remaining non-hydrogen bonds are counted one by one as: R-C, C-C, C-B, B-R' (upper), B-R' (right), O-O, for a total of 6 bonds.

method.method_draft: Scan the structure line by line. Exclude the vertical C-H bond and the O-H part of OH because the question excludes bonds involving hydrogen. Also ignore the curved arrow(s). Count the remaining non-H bonds: R-C, C-C, C-B, B-R' top, B-R' right, and O-O. Total = 6.
